Without referring to the training material, explain the difference between the following four product categories:
I certify that I understand the Edwards products covered in this examination and can recognize their primary functions and intended applications based on the training material.
Should demonstrate understanding that panel/device capacity affects product selection and system design.
The deck states that heat detectors should not be relied upon as the sole means of fire protection and should be part of a broader life-safety approach.
CT1 = one Class B IDC / one SLC address; CT2 = one or two Class B IDCs / two SLC addresses.
CR = Form C dry-contact relay; CRH = high-voltage/high-current relay.
SB4 = standard 4-inch base; RB4 = relay base.
AB4GT = CO-compatible sounder base; AB4-LF = 520 Hz low-frequency audible base.
Signature duct smoke detector; SDH = duct detector housing assembly used with compatible Signature smoke detectors.
Air velocity should be verified to be within the detector's specified operating range, including direction of airflow.
The deck identifies the APS as having the same wiring/internal characteristics as the BPS while providing more available room for amplifiers and modules.
SIGA-HRD — fixed-temperature and rate-of-rise heat detection.
Duct smoke detection — products such as SIGA-SD, SIGA-DDOS, or the SIGA-SDH housing/application should be considered based on the specific system requirement.
SIGA-CRH — addressable high-power control relay designed for high-voltage/high-current relay applications.
G4S/G4SV — confirm speaker/strobe requirements, 25/70 VRMS requirements, speaker wattage/voltage settings, and strobe requirements.
Responses should demonstrate an understanding of the basic roles of the four categories rather than simply repeating product names.
